note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a ARM 13; A06b ARM 13; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 3 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Dual citizenship restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Dual citizenship restriction), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a dual-citizenship restriction on descent, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.said: Person has been lawfully resident in Armenia for 3 years. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... Dual citizenship restriction ... Person is born to parents who are both citizens or to a parent who is a citizen and the other parent is unknown or stateless. If one parent is a citizen and the other parent is a foreigner, the child acquires citizenship based on a written consent. In the absence of written consent, the child acquires citizenship if s/he is otherwise stateless, or both parents reside permanently in Armenia. ... Dual citizenship restriction ...
